title: Does NP-hardness of MCSP imply circuit lower bounds for EXP?
formal: If the Minimum Circuit Size Problem is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions, must \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subset \mathrm{P}\)/poly? The hypothesis uses unrestricted ordinary polynomial-time reductions, with no locality, uniform-\(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\) or naturalness promise.

context:
MCSP tests whether an explicit truth table has a small circuit. An NP-hardness proof would relate efficient reductions to the same lower bounds that the output instances ask us to establish.

The source derives \(\mathrm{EXP}\ne \mathrm{NP}\cap \mathrm{P}\)/poly, and consequently \(\mathrm{EXP}\ne \mathrm{ZPP}\), from ordinary polynomial-time NP-hardness. These statements do not assert that EXP itself lacks polynomial-size circuits.

The original source also discusses stronger restrictions on reductions. The retained card selects the general implication to \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subset \mathrm{P}\)/poly and does not combine it with the separate uniform-\(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\) reduction conjecture.

sentences: MCSP asks whether a fully listed Boolean function has a small circuit.
The question concerns what proving its ordinary NP-hardness would force elsewhere in complexity theory.
The proposed consequence is that some exponential-time language requires superpolynomial circuits.
Existing consequences separate EXP from smaller intersections or randomized classes and do not yield that circuit lower bound.
The target captures a major proposed connection between metacomplexity and nonuniform lower bounds.

definitions: An MCSP input is the complete truth table \(t\in \{0,1\}^{2^{n}}\) of a Boolean function on \(n\ge 1\) input bits, in lexicographic order, together with a nonnegative integer size threshold s in binary. It is accepted if some Boolean circuit of size at most s computes that function. Circuits are finite acyclic graphs over binary AND and OR, unary NOT, input variables and constants 0,1, with one designated output and unrestricted sharing. Size counts noninput gates, including constant gates. The total encoded input length counts the truth table, threshold and delimiters. Invalid encodings are rejected. NP-hardness means that for every language L in NP there is a deterministic polynomial-time map r such that \(x\in \mathrm{L}\) iff \(r(x)\in\)MCSP. NP consists of languages accepted by nondeterministic polynomial-time Turing machines. \(\mathrm{EXP}=\bigcup _{k\ge 1}\mathrm{DTIME}(2^{n^{k}}); \mathrm{P}\)/poly consists of languages decided by families of Boolean circuits whose sizes are bounded by a polynomial in input length, with no uniformity condition on their construction. \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subset \mathrm{P}\)/poly means that some language in EXP has no such polynomial-size circuit family.
answer_criterion: Prove the conditional implication or its logical negation in these exact reduction and circuit models. Deriving only \(\mathrm{EXP}\ne \mathrm{ZPP}\) or \(\mathrm{EXP}\ne \mathrm{NP}\cap \mathrm{P}\)/poly is a weaker consequence. A theorem for a restricted reduction class or for partial, promise or approximate circuit minimization does not prove the stated implication.
